evals.prompt: I can't describe the visual style I want for our new admin dashboard. Just show me a bunch of real options so I can point at what's close.
evals.expected_output: Generates a batch of visibly distinct options (not near-identical variants) rather than asking the user to describe an abstract style they already said they can't articulate.
expectations: Does not ask the user to describe the abstract style in words given they already said they can't
Generates multiple genuinely distinct options rather than one guess or minor variations of the same idea
Presents the options with enough distinction that a real choice is possible

evals.prompt: Here's our existing product's screenshots and our current brand color (a specific teal). Generate style directions for a new settings page that still feels like the same product.
evals.expected_output: Reads and treats the existing screenshots/brand color as the starting vocabulary, generating directions that build on the existing identity rather than proposing unrelated fresh concepts.
expectations: Inspects the provided existing screenshots/brand color before generating anything
Generated options are recognizably related to the existing product identity, not disconnected fresh concepts
Does not discard or ignore the stated brand color without the user asking to

evals.prompt: Give me some color intensity options for this dashboard — I want to see the range from pretty muted to pretty bold.
evals.expected_output: Generates a real vertical ladder across the color-intensity axis (e.g. several distinct intensity steps), not just two extremes or a single 'medium' option.
expectations: Generates multiple distinct steps along the color-intensity axis, not just two endpoints
The steps are genuinely visually distinguishable from each other, not near-duplicates
Covers the requested range from muted to bold, not just one end of it

evals.prompt: I said I want it less colorful, but don't just make it black and white — I still want it to feel like our brand.
evals.expected_output: Correctly interprets 'less colorful' as fewer competing focal points / better color-role discipline rather than desaturating everything to grayscale, per the skill's own explicit distinction.
expectations: Does not interpret 'less colorful' as a literal black-and-white/grayscale treatment
Preserves the brand's color identity while reducing competing focal points
Explains or demonstrates the actual change as a color-role adjustment, not blanket desaturation

evals.prompt: Here are the 6 options you generated. Just show them all to me now, I'm ready to pick.
evals.expected_output: Reviews the generated options itself first (marking which look too generic, too colorful, closest to target, etc.) before presenting them, rather than dumping all 6 with no curation.
expectations: Reviews/opens the generated images itself before presenting them
Provides a short decision note or characterization for each option (e.g. too dead, too colorful, closest to target)
Does not present a raw, uncurated dump of file paths with no guidance

evals.prompt: I like option H02's color placement and option V04's palette intensity best. Combine those two into the actual implementation.
evals.expected_output: Extracts and fuses the specific named principles (H02's color placement, V04's intensity) from the two selected references, rather than trying to literally copy pixels from either generated image.
expectations: Explicitly references combining the two named options' specific attributes (color placement from one, intensity from the other)
Implements based on extracted principles (color roles, layout density) rather than attempting pixel-level reproduction
The result is a coherent fusion, not just one option with the other ignored

evals.prompt: These three generated options you're about to show me all kind of look like siblings — barely different from each other.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes insufficient contrast between options as a real problem and regenerates at least one with clearer differentiation, rather than presenting near-identical options as if they were meaningfully distinct choices.
expectations: Acknowledges that near-identical options don't serve the goal of exposing a real taste boundary
Regenerates or revises at least one option for clearer contrast rather than presenting the flawed batch as-is
Does not claim the near-identical options represent genuinely different directions

evals.prompt: I want you to evolve our existing UI to feel fresher, but don't throw away the current layout and components — just the visual treatment.
evals.expected_output: Generates options that evolve the existing UI's visual treatment while explicitly preserving the current layout/components, rather than proposing a from-scratch redesign that discards existing assets.
expectations: Preserves the existing layout and component structure per the explicit request
Changes are scoped to visual treatment (color, style) rather than a full redesign
Does not propose discarding current assets when the user explicitly asked to keep them
